1.signage:
800 graves without a name.
International conflict. American blood on European soil. War against fascism. Ask a random person what war the above is describing, and most will pick World War II. Few would pick the Spanish Civil War of 1936-1939. Fewer would think that isolationist America would have anything to do with a rebellion in a European nation. Yet, 2,800 Americans—soldiers, civilians, nurses, drivers, men and women—woke to the sound of encroaching fascism on the world, five years before their government ever did. 800 would never return. Amongst them, 81 sons and daughters of Massachusetts.
Welcome to the story of the 15th International Brigade: the 58th Abraham Lincoln Battalion, and the stories of 2,800 American volunteers who disobeyed their government to fight in Europe before World War II. This Museum is dedicated to preserving the stories of these men and women, and the cause they fought for.
We kindly ask you to approach the exhibits respectfully, and feel free to ask any questions to our volunteer staff.
